run.question:
Alertmanager alert HighRequestErrorRate (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-26T08:03:34Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The HighRequestErrorRate alert for service_name frontend-proxy in otel-demo is driven by frontend-proxy error spans on GET and POST page/checkout requests that end as HTTP 504 after about 15.0 s. The 504s are frontend-proxy's own upstream timeout: its child span 'router frontend egress' carries error="true" and http.status_code="0", meaning no upstream response, and the traces place the frontend service (frontend-5c847cc9bd-k2rcf) as the upstream. The frontend accepts those requests and emits its own server span 'GET'/'POST' of about 15.0 s with no child spans and no status, and its own HTTP server metrics record only 200/308 completions (GET 200 = 3846, GET 308 = 440, POST 200 = 1022 over 10 minutes) with zero increase on both 500 series, so the requests are aborted unanswered rather than answered with an error. The evidence localizes the fault to the frontend's request handling rather than to a downstream dependency: completed downstream calls are fast (average span duration 2.24 ms product-catalog, 3.25 ms recommendation, 3.51 ms checkout, 0.83 ms ad), no downstream service shows error spans or any span over 10 s, and checkout completed all 193.91 PlaceOrder spans in the 10 minutes. The frontend pod is healthy by Kubernetes state (Running and Ready, 0 restarts, no terminated reason) and is not resource-saturated (working set 128.7 MB against a 250Mi limit, 0.048 CPU cores). Errors were zero through the 3-minute window ending 08:03:00 and then rose (66, 219.6, 308.4 per successive 3-minute window), after the namespace had been brought up at 07:55:02-07:55:05 and was serving 200s at 07:57:22-07:57:29. The internal reason the frontend never finishes these requests is not observable with the available data, so the conclusion is partial and the root cause is named at the level of the frontend Deployment.

claims.text: The firing rule is group opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal, alert name HighRequestErrorRate, query sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0; the frontend-proxy instance had been firing since 2026-11-26T08:03:34.377Z with value 2.955 while the annotation states the threshold is 3.

frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans exist only for span_name GET and POST: increases over the authorized window to 08:06:06 were 311.45 for GET (60.32 by 08:04:06) and 23.63 for POST (0 by 08:04:06), against STATUS_CODE_UNSET increases of 3060.84 (GET) and 832.33 (POST); these are span counts, not unique request counts.

Across the namespace, STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in the window came only from frontend-proxy (GET/POST), load-generator (GET/POST, the client side of the same requests) and agent (ChatLLM.chat, LangGraph.workflow, POST /prompt and similar, steady about 2.19 then about 2.15 per window).

The frontend-proxy error spans are 504s of about 15.0 s: span_name GET/POST with status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code=ERROR, each having a child 'router frontend egress' span with error="true", http.status_code="0" and about 15.0 s duration.

The upstream frontend service (frontend-5c847cc9bd-k2rcf) creates its own span for those requests (span_name GET/POST, service frontend, duration 15.000-15.001 s, no status tags recorded) with no child span at all, ending about 0.2 ms before the frontend-proxy egress span ends, that is it is cut off by the client abort and never answers.

The frontend's own HTTP server metrics for the 10 minutes to 08:06:40 show GET 200 = 3846, GET 308 = 440, POST 200 = 1022 completed requests and an increase of 0 for both the GET and POST http_response_status_code="500" series, so no completed 5xx response was produced by the frontend.

Frontend span durations are bimodal: 847.8 'GET' and 41.6 'POST' root spans in the 10 minutes to 08:06:40, 507 frontend spans over 10 s, and zero frontend spans between 2 s and 10 s for every operation, including all oteldemo.* client calls, dns.lookup and tcp.connect.

In the 5-minute snapshot at 08:06:40 the only services with spans over 10 s were load-generator (1020), frontend-proxy (975), frontend (507) and agent (120); cart, checkout, currency, recommendation, ad, product-catalog, payment, shipping, email, image-provider, quote, mcp, chatbot, flagd and accounting had zero spans over 10 s, and average span duration was 2.24 ms for product-catalog, 3.25 ms recommendation, 3.51 ms checkout and 0.83 ms ad.

Checkout completed 193.91 oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans in the 10 minutes to 08:06:40, matching the frontend's client PlaceOrder spans (193.91), payment oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (193.91) and CartService/EmptyCart (193.91); currency returned 556.95 Convert spans all with STATUS_CODE_OK.

Traced failing requests are load-generator tasks user_browse_product (GET, 504), user_add_to_cart (GET, 504), user_get_recommendations (GET, 504) and user_checkout_single/user_checkout_multi (POST, 504); in the same window a user_view_cart GET of the frontend route /api/cart returned 200 in 5.8 ms and homepage-span 'GET /' averaged 4.18 ms.

Load-generator reports 438.45 GET error spans and 38.78 POST error spans against 2747.06 successful GET and 1819.52 successful POST spans in the 10 minutes to 08:06:40 (span counts, not unique requests); its task mix in the same window includes user_browse_product 1259.34, user_add_to_cart 685.15 and user_get_recommendations 358.73.

frontend-proxy error spans were 0 in every 3-minute window up to 08:03:00, then 66 (window ending 08:04:00), 219.6 (08:05:00) and 308.4 (08:06:00), so the deviation began around 08:01-08:03, about six minutes after the namespace came up.

All otel-demo workloads were brought up at 07:55:02-07:55:05: 26 Deployment 'ScalingReplicaSet' events with message 'Scaled up replica set ... from 0 to 1' plus Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started events, and all 26 otel-demo pods have startTime 07:55:02-07:55:05.

At startup the frontend served normally: its logs between 07:57:22 and 07:57:29 show 200 responses for /api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/recommendations and /api/checkout plus 'Order placed successfully'.

Kubernetes state shows no pod damage in otel-demo: every checked pod (frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout, currency, email, payment, product-catalog, recommendation, shipping) is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, container state running and no lastState.terminated reason; all three nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False; both CoreDNS pods are Running with 0 restarts.

The frontend container is not resource-saturated: working set 128,704,512 bytes at 08:06:40 with a peak of 129,564,672 bytes over the preceding 15 minutes against a 250Mi memory limit, and CPU rate 0.0482 cores averaged over 5 minutes at 08:06:40.

Service endpoints are not stale: the frontend Service endpoint 10.244.2.18 is exactly frontend-5c847cc9bd-k2rcf's pod IP and frontend-proxy's endpoint 10.244.2.69 is exactly frontend-proxy-77df9b8f7-4rjfb's pod IP, and no otel-demo endpoints object has notReadyAddresses.

No fault-injection setting is switched on in the otel-demo flagd ConfigMap demo.flagd.json: every listed flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, aiRunawayAgent, aiSlowResponse, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, failedReadinessProbe, imageSlowLoad, intlShippingSlowdown, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, productCatalogLockContention, recommendationCacheFailure, emitRawPii) has defaultVariant "off".

No otel-demo pod shows OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Failed evidence: the only Unhealthy event in the namespace is a readiness-probe miss on otel-collector-74d749ff5f-t8dl8 at 07:55:03 during startup (connection refused on port 13133), and no restart or termination is recorded on any container.

The blocking wait sits inside the frontend's own request path, before or during route handling: the request is accepted, the frontend root span is created, no child span ever starts, and the process stays nearly idle (0.048 cores) until the proxy aborts at 15 s.

Alternatively a single outbound call from the frontend never returns, which would leave exactly this signature because the unfinished client span is never exported; the telemetry cannot confirm or exclude this for cart, product-catalog, currency, recommendation, ad, checkout, payment, shipping or email, whose own span metrics show no errors and no spans over 10 s.

Capacity overload of the frontend by the load generator is not supported: while about 13.8% of load-generator GET spans failed, the frontend used only 0.048 CPU cores, stayed at 128.7 MB of its 250Mi limit, and completed its API requests in single-digit milliseconds.

Capture a stuck-request diagnostic from the frontend container (Node.js stack or heap dump, or per-request debug logging of page routes) to identify the exact call or lock that holds these requests open for the full 15 s, since page requests currently write no log line.

Read the frontend-proxy Envoy route/upstream timeout and circuit-breaker configuration from the container image or generated config to confirm the 15 s timeout that bounds these 504s, since the proxy container logged nothing and its config could not be read here.

gaps: The internal reason the frontend never completes these requests is not observable from the collected data: unfinished spans are never exported, the frontend writes no log line for page (non-/api) requests, and the error/warn regex log query over 08:03:00-08:06:46 (bad22b28-f6aa-4be6-8c7a-45096e8d811e-t1:c7932afb-fa24-49e1-8054-ea545e147357) returned no matching lines, a no_data view that only shows this query matched nothing.

No pre-incident baseline exists for frontend page latency: the whole otel-demo namespace was created at 07:55:02-07:55:05 and errors started around 08:01-08:03, so no comparable earlier period for the same pods is available.

frontend-proxy logs could not be inspected: the log fetch for that container returned 0 bytes read and no lines (728ca659-3168-44c7-b91b-fa339a8d6f6e-t0:9812b746-3944-4bb9-ba7e-2b7afc1eb1af, a no_data view), and its Envoy configuration is not readable with the available tools, so the 15 s timeout is inferred from span durations only.
Runtime flagd flag values as set through the flagd runtime/UI path cannot be read; only the ConfigMap defaults, all "off", were verified, so a runtime-only fault-flag toggle cannot be excluded.
Kubernetes events in otel-demo only cover 07:55:02-07:55:19 (startup); no events cover the ~08:01 onset, so no change at onset time could be verified.
The change_history integration is not configured, so no deploy or config-change record for the 07:55 bring-up or the 08:01 degradation could be checked.

Frontend span coverage is incomplete: most frontend-proxy page requests have no matching frontend root span (3185 load-generator GET spans versus 848 frontend 'GET' spans per 10 minutes), so span-based statements about the frontend describe only the exported subset.

No http_server_active_requests series and no per-route request metrics exist for the frontend page routes (queries 918874a4-f231-43ab-aa87-6cbcb48ec708-t1:bde2ea4b-02e0-4a28-b702-c3b857ddbbbd and 65fce833-d527-4b08-8598-ec0200621e6b-t0:d0d767a4-ecbb-431b-b6f5-5be377e6f19f returned no data), so concurrency and per-URL failure attribution for the frontend could not be measured.
next_steps: Take a Node.js stack or heap diagnostic, or enable page-route debug logging, inside frontend-5c847cc9bd-k2rcf while 504s are occurring to identify the blocking call.
Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy route configuration and upstream timeout/circuit-breaker settings in the running container.
Read the current flagd runtime flag values through its management interface to confirm no fault flag is enabled at run time.
Re-run the same environment from a known-good state to establish a frontend page-latency baseline for comparison.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
